title: Flat ringed complete equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $D(\mathcal O)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if, for every $U$ and $f\in\mathcal J(U)$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],N|_U)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise localization on the slice site over $U$. Use the same definition for $\mathcal J\mathcal B$. Assume $\mathcal B$ is flat over $\mathcal O$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and the induced map $\mathcal O/\mathcal J\to\mathcal B/\mathcal J\mathcal B$ is an isomorphism. Then restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] induces an equivalence between the full subcategories of locally derived complete objects in $D(\mathcal B)$ and $D(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence), with local completeness as in Tag 0999 (definition-derived-complete).

proof.text: Write $r$ for restriction of scalars. It is exact and conservative on module sheaves: kernels are sectionwise kernels with the inherited action, and cokernels are the same sheafifications of abelian presheaf cokernels before and after restriction. Thus it preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms of complexes, induces $r:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal O)$ by localization, and reflects isomorphisms (the cone has zero cohomology precisely when its underlying abelian sheaves do). By [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness], $r$ preserves and reflects the local completeness conditions, so it restricts to a functor between the stated full subcategories.

Restriction to a slice is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]. By the kernel and cokernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], this also proves exactness for module sheaves; consequently restriction preserves cohomology, quasi-isomorphisms, and quotient sheaves. Choose the augmented complex $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to\mathcal O[0]$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. Put $K_B^\bullet=K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal B$, with augmentation $\epsilon_B(x\otimes b)=\varphi(\epsilon(x))b$, and let $u:K^\bullet\to rK_B^\bullet$ be $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. These are chain maps and $r\epsilon_B\circ u=\varphi\circ\epsilon$. Flatness means tensoring is exact; applying this to the kernel/image sequences of any differential shows that this termwise tensor functor preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. On a slice where $\mathcal J$ has generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$, the augmented local description of $K$ therefore identifies $u$ with the comparison of extended Čech complexes: on each localization the identification sends $(a/f^n)\otimes b$ to $\varphi(a)b/\varphi(f)^n$, with inverse $b/\varphi(f)^n\mapsto(1/f^n)\otimes b$. The balancing relation and the relation making $f$ invertible show that these maps are well-defined and mutually inverse; sheafification gives the asserted sheaf maps. Finite products here are finite direct sums, so this also identifies all terms and differentials. The quotient-isomorphism hypothesis restricts to the slice, and flatness restricts to the slice by [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-extended-cech-comparison] there. Thus $u$ is locally a quasi-isomorphism and hence globally one: each cohomology kernel/cokernel sheaf vanishes on a covering family of these slices.

source.place: Tag 099I, construction of K and K prime; Tag 099H (lemma-map-identifies-koszul-and-cech-complexes).

proof.text: Fix this complex $K_B^\bullet$. For $E$ represented by $E^\bullet$, take the functorial K-injective replacement $E^\bullet\to I(E)^\bullet$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and define $F(E)$ by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal O}(rK_B^\bullet,I(E)^\bullet)$, giving it a $\mathcal B$-action by $(b h)(k)=h(bk)$. This is an action because $1h=h$, $(bc)h=b(ch)$ and addition distributes; restrictions commute with it, and the Hom differential is $\mathcal B$-linear since $d(bk)=b\,dk$. Maps are induced by the functorial maps of $I(E)$ and are $\mathcal B$-linear. For a quasi-isomorphism $v:E^\bullet\to\widetilde E^\bullet$, naturality gives $I(v)q_E=q_{\widetilde E}v$; since both replacement maps and $v$ are quasi-isomorphisms, two-out-of-three makes $I(v)$ a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] with $s=I(v)$ and $t=\mathrm{id}_{rK_B}$. Thus these Hom maps are quasi-isomorphisms when $E^\bullet\to\widetilde E^\bullet$ is one; they are so over $\mathcal B$ because the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves are unchanged. Hence localization gives a functor $F:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal B)$, whose restriction is naturally $rF(E)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(rK_B,E)$. This constructs the coefficient action and the functor; no equivalence or completeness is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 099I, displayed construction E prime = R SheafHom(r(K prime), E), with its coefficient action made explicit.

proof.text: Precomposition with $u$ gives a natural isomorphism $\theta_E:rF(E)\to R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,E)$: $u$ is the quasi-isomorphism proved in step 2 and [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] applies with $t=u$ and $s=\mathrm{id}_{I(E)}$, where the target replacement $I(E)$ is K-injective by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For locally derived complete $E$, the completion unit $\eta_E:E\to R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,E)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. Set $\alpha_E=\theta_E^{-1}\eta_E:E\to rF(E)$. It is a natural isomorphism. Its target is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete since its source is; [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness] then makes $F(E)$ locally derived $\mathcal J\mathcal B$-complete. Thus $F$ restricts to the proposed inverse functor and $\alpha$ gives one of the two required natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 099I, paragraph following the formula for E prime; Tag 099F, completion unit for a complete object.

proof.text: For a locally derived complete $M\in D(\mathcal B)$ construct $\beta_M:M\to F(rM)$ as follows. On a representing complex and its O-linear replacement $q:rM^\bullet\to I(rM)^\bullet$, send a homogeneous $m$ to the Hom cochain $k\mapsto q(\epsilon_B(k)m)$ (zero on degrees of $k$ other than zero). For $m$ of degree $n$, the Hom differential is $d_I\beta(m)(k)-(-1)^n\beta(m)(d_Kk)$. If $k$ has degree zero, this is $q(\epsilon_B(k)d_Mm)$; if $k$ has degree $-1$, the second term vanishes because $\epsilon_Bd_K=0$; in all other degrees both terms vanish. Therefore $d_{\mathrm{Hom}}\beta(m)=\beta(d_Mm)$. It is a chain map; it is B-linear because $\epsilon_B(bk)=b\epsilon_B(k)$, so $\beta_M(bm)(k)=q(\epsilon_B(k)bm)=\beta_M(m)(bk)$. Functoriality of $q$ makes it natural in chain maps, and the localization property in step 3 makes it natural in derived morphisms. Precomposing this cochain with $u$ yields $x\mapsto q(\varphi(\epsilon(x))m)=\epsilon(x)q(m)$, exactly the cochain defining $\eta_{rM}$ by precomposition with $\epsilon$. Thus $\theta_{rM}\circ r(\beta_M)=\eta_{rM}$ and $r(\beta_M)=\alpha_{rM}$. Step 4 applies since $rM$ is complete by [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness]. Hence $r(\beta_M)$ is an isomorphism. The conservativity proved in step 1 implies that $\beta_M$ is an isomorphism. The natural isomorphisms $\mathrm{id}\cong rF$ and $\mathrm{id}\cong Fr$ exhibit the asserted equivalence. This is the omitted final compatibility check in the source.
